scope.method: static source audit, SQLAlchemy metadata import, Alembic migration review, frontend route and proxy allowlist review

executive_conclusion.answer: Still an engineering platform, not yet a true product.
executive_conclusion.reason: The backend and DB contain many durable capabilities, and tenant scoping is mostly present for core business records. The frontend, however, exposes mostly read-only control-plane surfaces with engineering labels, disabled action shells, and missing workflows for organization management, execution, approvals, live gate writes, API keys, and record creation. Several backend APIs and DB-backed capabilities are hidden from the product UI or blocked by the frontend proxy allowlist.

interpretation.70_84: productizing but still missing complete workflow closure

database_alignment_audit.summary: Core C18 tenant scope is mostly persisted for jobs, artifacts, reviews, approvals, memory, operation logs, C17 observability, and C15 callback/DLQ state. Remaining risk is concentrated in transition/history rows, permission assignment scope, global identity/session state, static registries, and nonstandard shared-module scoping.

missing_org_id_tables.finding: Transition history has no org_id column and is not directly tenant-filterable by C18G loader criteria.
missing_org_id_tables.impact: Callback lifecycle history can become globally addressable unless every access joins through callback_state and enforces org scope.

missing_org_id_tables.finding: Assignments use scope_type and scope_key but no org_id column.
missing_org_id_tables.impact: Org-scoped permission rows rely on convention instead of DB-level tenant shape and are not automatically covered by C18G org filtering.

missing_org_id_tables.finding: Uses source_org_id and target_org_id instead of standard org_id.
missing_org_id_tables.impact: Legitimate cross-org model, but it is outside automatic org_id filtering and requires explicit query discipline.

schema_drift_from_c05_baseline.baseline: C05 created permission_registry, user_permission_assignments, and role_default_permissions.
schema_drift_from_c05_baseline.current: Permission assignments remain non-org_id scoped and rely on scope_type/scope_key; unified permission semantics now constrain owner access to platform admin/system categories instead of blanket owner full access.

schema_drift_from_c05_baseline.baseline: F07 core records were created without tenant scope.
schema_drift_from_c05_baseline.current: C18 migration added org_id to jobs, events, artifacts, reviews, approvals, memory, and operation logs.
execution_callbacks, execution_results, execution_dlq, callback_state, and dlq_state are DB-backed with org_id; callback_state_transitions lacks org_id.
event_streams, audit_logs, replay_jobs, anomaly_events, and storage_events are DB-backed with org_id, but query paths can fall back to platform/no explicit org filter.
ops alerts, canary, rollback, live gate policies, and unlock tokens are DB-backed with org_id.

backend_alignment_audit.summary: Backend has strong gating and durable support services, but actual execution remains mock/metadata-only. Many write APIs exist without frontend productization. Permission semantics are centralized, but C05 owner-full-access expectations and C18F/RBAC behavior are not fully aligned.

backend_capability_map.gap: Adapters are not executable implementations and are not product-managed.
